extracted.intended_audience: librarians, information professionals, and other professionals working in research-intensive environments worldwide
extracted.subtask_description: Description of the RDMLA online professional development curriculum: an 11-unit (plus two mini-modules) self‑paced course for librarians and research-support staff on essential research data management knowledge and skills.

rubrics_metrics.name: Essential RDM knowledge and skills
rubrics_metrics.description: Curriculum focuses on the essential knowledge and skills needed to collaborate effectively with researchers on data management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RDMLA features eleven online, self‑paced learning units and two mini‑modules designed to teach those core competencies; the curriculum is intended to enable effective collaboration with researchers on data management tasks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Course format: online, self-paced units
rubrics_metrics.description: The RDMLA curriculum is delivered as eleven online, self‑paced learning units plus two mini‑modules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Units are hosted on Canvas, enabling asynchronous completion; this affects learners' ability to fit the course into work schedules and the instructional design (modular learning).

rubrics_metrics.name: Open licensing and hosting
rubrics_metrics.description: RDMLA units are hosted online on Canvas under CC-BY-NC-SA (Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike) licensing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The CC‑BY‑NC‑SA license permits sharing and adaptation for noncommercial uses with attribution and requires derivatives to carry the same license; hosting on Canvas implies LMS-based delivery and possible institutional access considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language accessibility and inclusivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Core curriculum is available in Chinese and Spanish in addition to the original offering to increase access for non-English speakers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translation of core materials is an explicit program goal intended to broaden global accessibility for Chinese‑ and Spanish‑speaking librarians, information professionals, and researchers.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI for Librarians competency (ethical/practical integration)
rubrics_metrics.description: RDMLA: AI for Librarians emphasizes ethical, practical, and effective integration of generative AI tools into library and information science contexts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This mini/expanded offering targets emerging competencies at the intersection of AI and library practice, with explicit focus on ethics and practical application of generative AI in professional workflows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target audience and professional context
rubrics_metrics.description: Program is intended for librarians, information professionals, and other professionals working in research‑intensive environments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The curriculum is tailored to those who collaborate with researchers and operate in academic/health sciences/research library contexts; partner institutions listed (Harvard, Simmons, Boston University, etc.) reflect the research-intensive orientation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partnership and sponsorship as quality signals
rubrics_metrics.description: RDMLA is delivered through partnerships among an LIS academic program, academic health sciences and research libraries, and Elsevier, with multiple institutional partners and Elsevier sponsorship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The named partner institutions and sponsor are presented to indicate program credibility, domain relevance, and institutional support for curriculum content and delivery.
